Heard Sri Vishwaprakash who represents Sri Srinand A. Pachhapure, learned counsel on record for the appellant as well as Sri S.S.
Joshi learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

Aggrieved by the sum that is awarded as compensation by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi through orders in MVC 2669 of 2011 dated 17.11.2012, the claimant therein preferred the present appeal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant met with a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2011.

The appellant as a cleaner was earning Rs.15,000/-
per month by the date of accident.

However without considering the occupation and NC:
2025:KHC-D:15285 HC-KAR earnings of the appellant, the tribunal took the notional income of the appellant as Rs.150/- per day.
Learned counsel submits that very meager sum is awarded as compensation towards 'loss of future earnings' and no amount is awarded as compensation towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
Learned counsel states that as the appellant due to the injury sustained lost one of his lower limbs, the amount sought for may be granted.

4. The submission that is made by learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that the tribunal awarded justifiable sum as compensation under all heads, but in the light of the submission that is made by learned counsel for the appellant there may be marginal enhancement.
5.
It is not in dispute that the injury sustained due to the accident resulted in above amputation of the left lower limb of the appellant.
Considering the evidence produced, the tribunal rightly assessed the disability in respect of whole body as 55%.
So far as the income of the NC: 2025:KHC-D:15285 HC-KAR appellant is concerned, no substantive proof is produced.

However, basing on the submission that is made by learned counsel for the appellant, that for the relevant period of accident Sidray Ravasab Tavanshi vs Mainunddin Nabisab Mulla on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176170410/
2 i.e. for the year 2011, the High Court Legal Services Committee, Dharwad Bench is taking the notional income as Rs.6,000/- per month, this Court considers desirable to adopt the said figure.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the appellant was aged around 32 years by the date of accident.
Thus the appellant is required to lead the rest of his long life with only one lower limb.
It will be very difficult for him to continue his occupation either as cleaner or by doing any other thing to eke out his livelihood.
Therefore this Court is of the view that future prospects are required to be added.

As the appellant was aged around 32 years by the date of accident, 40% of the earnings are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus taking the notional income of (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC:
2025:KHC-D:15285 HC-KAR the appellant as Rs.6,000/- per month, on adding 40% towards future prospects, on applying the appropriate multiplier '16' and the disability in respect of whole body as 55%, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to receive towards 'loss of future earnings' is as under:
Notional monthly income Rs.6,000/-
 Annual income Rs.72,000/-
 On adding 40% towards future Rs.1,00,800/-
 prospects  On applying appropriate multiplier Rs.16,12, 800/-
 '16'
 Loss of future earnings, disability in Rs.8,87,040/-
 respect of whole body being 55%.
6.
Thus, the appellate is entitled to a sum of Rs.8,87,040/- towards 'loss of future earnings'.
However the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,75,000/- only.

Thus the enhancement under said head will be Rs.4,12,040/-
(Rs.8,87,040/- minus Rs.4,75,000/-).
7.

Having considered the fact that the appellant underwent a surgery and during the course of surgery, above knee amputation of the left lower limb was done, this Court is of the view that the appellant could not have NC: 2025:KHC-D:15285 HC-KAR attended his normal pursuits at least for a period of 8 months.

Thus 'loss of earnings during laid up period' comes to Rs.48,000/-
(Rs.6,000/- X 8).
The Tribunal failed to award any sum towards 'loss of earnings during laid up period'.
Therefore the total sum which the appellant is entitled to receive in addition to the sum that is awarded by the tribunal is Rs.4,60,040/- (Rs.4,12,040/- plus Rs.48,000/-).

Therefore the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation that is granted by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi, through orders in MVC 2669 of 2011 dated 17.11.2012 is enhanced Sidray Ravasab Tavanshi vs Mainunddin Nabisab Mulla on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176170410/
3 by Rs.4,60,040/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit, except for the period of delay of 481 days as per the order dated 02.02.2015.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:15285 HC-KAR (iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
